chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Malik, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), informing my master that a son of my brother had died and bequeathed a farm to my master. He also bequeathed that everything in his house, even the pegs, should be sold and the price brought to my master. He bequeathed a pilgrimage, bequeathed to the poor of his family, and bequeathed property to his aunt and sister. I said: I looked and found that what he bequeathed was more than one-third, perhaps approaching half of what he left. He left a son of three years and left a debt. My master saw this and ruled: One should limit his bequest to one-third of his wealth, and that portion should be distributed among those he bequeathed to according to their shares, if God wills.
ai.seo_question: How is an estate distributed when the total bequests exceed one-third of the total wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the Shia jurisprudence of 'al-thaluth' (the one-third limit) for bequests, establishing that when total legacies exceed this threshold, they are reduced proportionally rather than being applied sequentially. It highlights the Imam's practical application of this rule in complex estates involving multiple beneficiaries, including non-heirs like an aunt and sister, while accounting for debts and a minor heir. This ruling underscores the balance between honoring the deceased's wishes and preserving the mandatory shares of the heirs.
